title: NY State Assembly · District 67
area: Manhattan's Upper West Side, roughly from West 59th Street to West 97th Street between Central Park West and the Hudson River, including Lincoln Square and Manhattan Valley

context.text: Incumbent Linda Rosenthal is unopposed on the November ballot. The Democratic, Republican, Conservative Party, and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for June 23, 2026 were all canceled; Rosenthal advanced from the Democratic and Working Families Party lines without appearing on the ballot, and the only Republican/Conservative candidate, Mike Muñoz, withdrew or was disqualified before the primary.

candidates.name: Linda Rosenthal
candidates.currentRole: Member, NY State Assembly, District 67 (since 2006); Chair, Assembly Housing Committee

summary.text: Linda Rosenthal has represented Assembly District 67 on Manhattan's Upper West Side since 2006 and chairs the Assembly Housing Committee. She is unopposed for re-election in 2026.

background.text: Rosenthal earned a B.A. in history from the University of Rochester in 1980.
Before her election to the Assembly, she worked as Manhattan director of special projects for the office of U.S. Representative Jerrold Nadler from 1992 to 2006.
She has served as a delegate to the Democratic National Convention and as president of the Community Free Democrats political club.

In the 2025-2026 legislative session she chairs the Housing Committee and also sits on the Agriculture, Codes, and Health committees; she previously chaired the Social Services Committee (2021-2022) and the Alcoholism and Drug Abuse Committee (2017, 2019-2020).

priorities.text: On banning the shackling of pregnant people in police custody: "The shackling of pregnant women is nothing short of barbaric. New York State has taken steps over the years to protect new mothers from this inhumane treatment, but a glaring loophole has left individuals who are simply in the custody of law enforcement without any protections."

On her health data privacy legislation: "New Yorkers have a right to keep their private data private, and this bill will prevent companies from using their most sensitive health information without permission. No one, from faceless third parties to giant tech companies, has an inherent right to use information about someone's last period, heart rate, step count or health-related search histories."

On protecting medical providers who follow state (rather than federal) vaccine guidance: "Resisting the Trump Administration means introducing and passing legislation that insulates New Yorkers from his dangerous policies... I am proud that my legislation will give people across the state, including the very medical professionals who've spent their lives protecting the public good, access to life-saving vaccines."

positions.summary: Sponsored legislation protecting reproductive-health data from sale to third parties, framing it as protection against federal restrictions on reproductive rights.
positions.quote: The Trump Administration has already proven itself to be a lethal force against reproductive rights and gender-affirming care in the United States. My legislation safeguards sensitive information that could easily be weaponized by an overzealous and punitive federal or state government.

positions.summary: Sponsored the New York Health Information Privacy Act barring sale of health data without consent, and legislation shielding providers who administer vaccines under state or local guidance.
positions.quote: This bill ensures that our personal health data will not be sold to the highest bidder.

positions.summary: Sponsored A.1777, which was passed in the state budget and bans the manufacture of 3D-printed guns and the dissemination of 3D gun-printing files in New York.

As Housing Committee chair, announced passage of a budget provision raising the income-eligibility limits for the Senior Citizen Rent Increase Exemption (SCRIE) and Disability Rent Increase Exemption (DRIE), which cap rent increases for eligible low-income seniors and people with disabilities.

record.text: Sponsored A.1670-B, extending the existing ban on shackling incarcerated pregnant and postpartum women to those in law enforcement custody (police stations, prosecutors' offices, and other holding facilities); it passed both houses in June 2026.

Sponsored the New York Health Information Privacy Act (A.10357), prohibiting the sale of New Yorkers' health data collected by apps and digital devices without consumer consent; passed the Assembly and Senate.
Announced passage of a Revenue budget bill provision she sponsored raising SCRIE/DRIE income-eligibility limits for rent-increase exemptions for seniors and people with disabilities.
Sponsored A.1777, banning the manufacture of 3D-printed guns and dissemination of 3D gun-printing files, which passed as part of the New York State budget.
Sponsored A.9140, extending liability protections to health care providers who administer vaccines under state or local guidance rather than federal recommendations; passed the Assembly.
Sponsored A.1740, requiring New York State to provide free menstrual products in state-owned or state-leased buildings.
Voted yes on S.3460, granting employees access to their personnel records; passed the Assembly 92-49.

researchNotes: Rosenthal has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and has no declared opponent, so her priorities and positions here are drawn from her official legislative press releases rather than campaign materials. Record items cover the current 2025-2026 session; her full multi-decade sponsorship history was not comprehensively reviewed.
